lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Linh, it's Rachel. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sounds good to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How's your body feeling this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay. The heat is getting to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you hit your goal this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: It went really well, I actually did it 4 times.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people walk inside the mall early, before the stores open. It's cool and it's flat.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You figured that out on your own.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you use the step counter?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. I just didn't feel like it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hmm, I have to think about that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walking fit in your day?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: This heat is killing me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd be out there if you could find a time of day that doesn't feel like an oven.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It feels like a lot right now.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walking fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My mom is staying with us and I'm taking care of her.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: With all the rain I just stayed in.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's not that you don't want to walk, it's that the weather keeps winning.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, getting started makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the walking going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, it's been so hot, by 9 in the morning you can't be outside. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Just get out there, even when it's hot.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to walk 30 minutes on 4 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 5.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 5 and not a 2?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the heat gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll do it right when I wake up, before anything else.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Reframes participant's goal as starting small; not their words
Credits participant with an idea the coach offered
Repeats earlier question instead of exploring the Monday-Friday plan
Directive push right after participant voiced barriers

flags.reason: Directive 'Just get out there' after participant described heat and knee barriers; undermines autonomy and invites resistance.
Participant says walking hurts knees; coach moved to 'completely your call' without exploring the pain or change talk.
Concrete commitment (Mon/Wed/Fri) was not reinforced or explored; coach repeated an earlier question instead.

score.summary: Coach used good open questions and reflections early, and the participant produced substantial change talk around their health and their plan. However, the coach asked repeatedly about the same barriers, gave an unsolicited directive at line 52, and did not explore the knee pain or the participant's own commitments.
strengths: Line 3: opened by asking what the participant wanted to cover, setting an agenda.
Line 40 and 42: complex reflections linked the weather barrier to the participant's love for family and wellbeing.
Line 57-61: used a confidence ruler and backup-plan question to build a realistic goal.
coaching_tips: Line 52: replace 'Just get out there' with a question such as 'What might make an early walk work for you?' to avoid persuading.
Line 45: explore the knee pain ('Tell me more about the knees') before moving on, since it may be a barrier to address with a clinician.
Line 36: instead of repeating the earlier question, reflect the Monday/Wednesday/Friday commitment at line 35 and ask what would make it happen.
Line 16 and 17: build on the 'I need this for my head' statement with a deeper question about what matters most to them.
Line 63: close with a brief summary of the participant's own reasons and plan before setting the next contact.
